p: You can't talk about Coventry without mentioning Lady Godiva, who, according to legend, rode naked through the streets to protest against her husband's taxes. There's a statue of her in Broadgate, just a short walk from the Lower Precinct, and the Godiva clock nearby has figures that appear on the hour.

Coventry was UK City of Culture in 2021, and the city has plenty of public art and creative spaces to show for it. FarGo Village, just outside the ring road, is a quirky creative quarter with independent shops, street food and events, and it's well worth a wander.
For a taste of old Coventry, head to Spon Street, where medieval timber-framed buildings have been preserved and rebuilt to give a glimpse of what the city looked like before the wartime bombing.

When it's time for some fresh air, War Memorial Park, south of the centre, is a big, popular park with play areas, a splash park in the summer and plenty of space. A short drive east, Coombe Abbey Country Park has woodland walks, a lake and lovely gardens around the historic abbey building.
The Coventry Canal Basin, on the northern edge of the centre, is a peaceful spot where you can see narrowboats and enjoy a stroll along the towpath.
The city centre is compact, so once you've parked, most places are walkable, which makes it an easy and affordable day out.
